1.question: What is Nibbana?
1.plain: Nibbana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.
1.text:
This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all
preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of
craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.
1.note: motto refrain complete (standard rendering only; alternative lives in A). Head 695.5->696.8: whisper word-times put chant-tail to 694.9, 'This' at 696.9

2.question: Why don't I see Nibbana right now?
2.plain: You do not see Nibbana right now because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.
text: Due to the very ignorance of the fact that it is seeing because it is looking, the dog imagines another dog, there, in the water. What is called maññanā is an imagining of that sort.
Only a looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen. Apart from the bare act of hearing, there is nothing to be heard.
There is no seer, apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathāgata... For the worldling, the bare act of seeing carries with it a perception of 'one who sees'.
2.note: TRIPLE pointer (owner 2026-10-28: all three in essay-0): manana defines the disease / only-looking shows it / no-seer names it. Each opens+closes clean (whisper word-times). Dog simile stays as the S2 beat.

3.question: What keeps it going?
3.plain: Thirst keeps it going: impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage. The gap is ignored. What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst.
3.text:
Impelled by that imagining, it runs towards the mirage... The gap is
ignored... What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.
3.note: craving sentence only (dangle trimmed: next sentence starts 1869.8)

4.question: How is the sense of self constructed?
4.plain: The sense of self is constructed like this: when one looks into a mirror one suddenly becomes self-conscious. Even with no such notion, the moment one looks one is reminded of it, as if to exclaim: 'Ah, here I am!'
4.text:
It is when one looks into a mirror that one suddenly becomes self-
conscious... Even if one already has no such notion, the moment one looks
into a mirror one is suddenly reminded of it, as if to exclaim: 'Ah,
here I am!'
4.note: mirror moment + mechanism naming (conceit-I from five grasping groups; closes before Pali philology 2233+)

5.question: How is Nibbana attained?
5.plain: Nibbana is only attained now: in seeing, just the seeing, with no I added. Then it will not carry you. Nothing to stand on, nowhere to land — neither here, nor there, nor in between. This itself is the end of suffering.
5.text: In the seen there will be just the seen... Then you will not be by it. And when you are not by it, you are not in it. And when you are not in it, you are neither here nor there nor in between. This itself is the end of suffering.
5.note: Bahiya formula, DS-verified sentence start through "end of suffering" (was YT-time; L14 offset = YT-DS 10.0s), credit excluded

6.question: What is Nibbana like?
6.plain: like a flame with no fuel.
6.text: I am grown cool, extinguished as I am.
